translation_en:
Li Rui 李銳: Registered in Liangzhou Guard, Shaanxi, originally from Xingan County, Jiangxi; a National University Student specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji), style name Wensheng, eighth in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-six, born on the fifteenth day of the intercalary seventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuanchu, his grandfather Zhongyong, his father Weizhi, his principal mother née Yang, and his birth mother née Feng. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Zhengxuan, Zhengxu, Zhao, Xuan, Zhenghe, Qin, and Zheng, and his younger brother is Yue. He married a woman née Xu. He placed fifteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Tingfang 楊廷芳: Registered in a civilian household of Shaoyang County, Baoqing Prefecture, Huguang; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), style name Mengren, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanwang, his grandfather Wei (Vice Prefect of Ningzhou), his father Heng (Recorder of Gaoyou Subprefecture), and his mother née Zhang. His mother is living. His younger brother is Tingxiu. He married a woman née Li. He placed one hundred thirty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Rui 趙銳: Registered in a civilian household of Xiuwu County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing), style name Yizhi, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Deming, his grandfather Youliang, his father Wang, his mother née Niu, and his stepmother née Shi. His father is living. His younger brother is Qin (a Tribute Student of the jimao year [1459]). He married a woman née Yan, and subsequently married a woman née Jiang. He placed tenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zhe 劉哲: Registered in a military household of Baishui County, Tongzhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi; a National University Student specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), style name Guangzhe, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-three, born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yanming, his grandfather Wen, his father Yun (District Magistrate), and his mother née Ma. Both of his parents are living. His younger brother is Guangqi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xi 王璽 [registered in a military household in Changyuan County, Kaizhou, Daming Prefecture, Zhili; National University Student; specialized in the Classic of Odes (Shijing); courtesy name Dayong 大用; first in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth month]. title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕惟治天下亦
多術矣舉而行之必有
其要傳謂禮樂刑政四
達而不悖則王道備然
則其要固不出此四者
===
而行之亦有先後緩急
之序歟唐虞三代所以
措天下於雍熙泰和之
盛者率用此道可歷指
其實而詳言之歟後之

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
王一夔
臣對臣聞帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於誠
盖誠為道之實而道即禮樂刑政之理也禮樂
而非誠無以立其體刑政而非誠無以達其用
惟其誠也由是而制禮作樂則禮備而樂和由
是而明刑脩政則刑清而政舉故善為治者未
有不本於道善行道者未有不本於誠二帝之
所以帝天下而世躋雍熈者此誠也三王之所
以王天下而俗臻康乂者亦此誠也下逮漢唐
宋之英君誼辟所以不能比隆於二帝三王而
===
治不古若者庸非此心之誠有或間歟大哉誠
乎其為萬化之本原萬事之樞紐人君為治之
大本乎欽惟
皇帝陛下聰明先物睿智有臨法二帝三王之要道
紹
祖宗列聖之宏規曩者嗣大厯服不迩聲色不殖貨
利凡耳目之娱珎異之獻悉誠心罷去與民休
息是以十五年間
朝廷清明民物熈皥四時調玉燭之和萬彙賛禎
祥之應属者順

王一夔

臣對：臣聞帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於誠。盖誠為道之實，而道即禮樂刑政之理也。禮樂而非誠，無以立其體；刑政而非誠，無以達其用。惟其誠也，由是而制禮作樂，則禮備而樂和；由是而明刑脩政，則刑清而政舉。故善為治者，未有不本於道；善行道者，未有不本於誠。二帝之所以帝天下而世躋雍熈者，此誠也；三王之所以王天下而俗臻康乂者，亦此誠也。下逮漢、唐、宋之英君誼辟，所以不能比隆於二帝三王，而治不古若者，庸非此心之誠有或間歟？大哉誠乎！其為萬化之本原、萬事之樞紐、人君為治之大本乎！欽惟皇帝陛下，聰明先物，睿智有臨，法二帝三王之要道，紹祖宗列聖之宏規。曩者嗣大厯服，不迩聲色，不殖貨利，凡耳目之娱、珎異之獻，悉誠心罷去，與民休息。是以十五年間，朝廷清明，民物熈皥，四時調玉燭之和，萬彙賛禎祥之應。属者順
translation_en:
Wang Yikui 王一夔

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way, and the Way of emperors and kings is rooted in sincerity. For sincerity is the substance of the Way, and the Way is the principle underlying ritual, music, punishments, and administration. If ritual and music lack sincerity, there is nothing by which to establish their substance; if punishments and administration lack sincerity, there is nothing by which to extend their function. Only through sincerity, when one thereby institutes rituals and creates music, are rituals complete and music harmonious; when one thereby clarifies punishments and cultivates administration, are punishments pure and administration upheld. Therefore, among those skilled at governing, there has never been one who did not root it in the Way; among those skilled at practicing the Way, there has never been one who did not root it in sincerity. That by which the Two Emperors ruled the world as emperors and raised the age to harmonious prosperity was this sincerity; that by which the Three Kings ruled the world as kings and brought customs to peace and order was also this sincerity. Coming down to the heroic rulers and righteous sovereigns of the Han, Tang, and Song, the reason they could not match the splendor of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and their governance did not equal antiquity—was it not because the sincerity of their minds had moments of interruption? Great indeed is sincerity! Is it not the source of the myriad transformations, the pivot of the myriad affairs, and the great foundation of a ruler's governance?

I reverently reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor, with intelligence anticipating all things and sagely wisdom overseeing all, models himself on the essential Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, and continues the grand plans of the Imperial Ancestors and successive sages. Previously, upon inheriting the great succession, you did not approach sensual pleasures of music and women, nor did you accumulate goods and wealth; all amusements of the ears and eyes and tributes of rare curiosities were abolished with a sincere heart, allowing the people to rest and recover. Thus, for fifteen years, the court was pure and bright, the people and all things were prosperous and content, the four seasons regulated the harmony of the Jade Candle, and the myriad beings aided the response of auspicious omens. title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
天應人復登
寶位乾坤為之再造人紀為之肇脩禮樂明備刑政
脩舉普天之下莫不謳歌乎鳳儀獸舞之治率
土之濱莫不甄陶於鳶飛魚躍之天治效之盛
振古而無以加矣是皆本於
皇上至誠行道之所致也茲猶不自滿假乃渙
綸音下
明詔進臣等於
廷降賜
清問首之以禮樂刑政施為緩急之序繼之以唐
===
虞三代漢唐宋治化隆替之由終之以所以用
禮樂刑政而克臻帝王治效之道至哉
問也顧臣愚陋曷足以上揆
淵衷雖然天道下濟而光明地道卑而上行
陛下既誠心發策以下問矣臣敢不悉心披誠以上
對乎竊惟帝王治天下之術非一端也然所行
之要不越乎禮樂刑政而已盖禮有三千三百
之儀所以節民之心使其所行無過不及焉樂
有五音六律之作所以和民之聲使其所言無
所乖戾焉故曰安上治民莫善於禮移風易俗

天應人，復登寶位，乾坤為之再造，人紀為之肇脩，禮樂明備，刑政脩舉。普天之下，莫不謳歌乎鳳儀獸舞之治；率土之濱，莫不甄陶於鳶飛魚躍之天。治效之盛，振古而無以加矣！是皆本於皇上至誠行道之所致也。茲猶不自滿假，乃渙綸音，下明詔，進臣等於廷，降賜清問：首之以禮樂刑政施為緩急之序，繼之以唐虞三代、漢、唐、宋治化隆替之由，終之以所以用禮樂刑政而克臻帝王治效之道。至哉問也！顧臣愚陋，曷足以上揆淵衷？雖然，天道下濟而光明，地道卑而上行。陛下既誠心發策以下問矣，臣敢不悉心披誠以上對乎？

竊惟帝王治天下之術非一端也，然所行之要不越乎禮樂刑政而已。盖禮有三千三百之儀，所以節民之心，使其所行無過不及焉；樂有五音六律之作，所以和民之聲，使其所言無所乖戾焉。故曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮；移風易俗，
translation_en:
…with Heaven and responding to mankind, Your Majesty has reascended the Precious Throne. Heaven and earth have thereby been remade; human relationships have thereby been newly ordered; rites and music are brilliant and complete; punishments and governance are well-regulated and upheld. Beneath the whole expanse of heaven, there is none who does not sing the praises of a rule in which phoenixes come with stately demeanor and beasts dance; to the furthest shores of the land, there is none who is not molded and nurtured under a sky where hawks fly and fishes leap. The flourishing efficacy of Your governance surpasses anything since antiquity! All of this stems from the fact that Your Majesty practices the Way with the utmost sincerity. Yet, still not content or self-satisfied, You have proclaimed Your silken words and sent down a luminous edict, summoning Your servants to the Court and graciously bestowing Your clear inquiry: beginning with the sequence of relative urgency in implementing rites, music, punishments, and governance; continuing with the reasons for the rise and decline of transformative rule in the eras of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], the Three Dynasties, Han, Tang, and Song; and concluding with the Way by which rites, music, punishments, and governance may be employed so as to attain the governing efficacy of the ancient emperors and kings. How supreme is this inquiry! Considering how foolish and rustic Your servant is, how could I be worthy of fathoming the depths of Your imperial mind above? Even so, the Way of Heaven reaches downward and shines brightly, while the Way of Earth is lowly yet ascends upward. Since Your Majesty has posed this policy question in all sincerity to inquire of those below, how could Your servant dare not pour out his whole heart and lay bare his sincerity to reply to You above?

Your servant humbly observes that the arts by which emperors and kings govern All-under-Heaven are not of a single kind, yet the essentials of what they put into practice do not go beyond rites, music, punishments, and governance. For rites have their three thousand and three hundred rules of ceremony, which serve to regulate the minds of the people so that their conduct neither exceeds nor falls short; music has its compositions of the five tones and six pitch-pipes, which serve to harmonize the voices of the people so that their words have nothing perverse or discordant in them. Therefore it is said: "For securing the rulers above and governing the people, nothing is better than rites; for changing prevailing habits and transforming customs,…

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
莫善於樂是禮樂所以教民而為出治之本
陛下所謂先與急者在是也若夫政者法制禁令也
所以一民之行而率其倦怠焉刑者墨劓剕宮
大辟也所以防民之奸而懲其恣肆焉故曰道
之以政齊之以刑民免而無耻是刑政所以弼
教而為輔治之具
陛下所謂後與緩者在是也雖然禮樂刑政固有先
後緩急之序要之亦不可以偏廢也使有禮樂
而無刑政則徒善不足以為治使有刑政而無
禮樂則徒法不能以自行故傳謂禮樂刑政四
===
達而不悖則王道備誠哉是言也稽之於古唐
虞之時以言其禮則五禮備而三禮明以言其
樂則六律和而八音諧禮樂於是乎大備焉德
惟善政政在養民而六府三事之允治明于五
刑刑期無刑而五服三就之克允刑政於是乎
大彰焉是以當時萬邦協和而黎民有於變之
休庶績咸熈而四夷有来王之效豈非唐虞能
用禮樂刑政而致雍熈泰和之盛乎然推其所
由則又本於堯之允恭克讓舜之温恭允塞之
所致也夏商之世司徒脩六禮以節民性樂正

陛下所謂後與緩者在是也雖然禮樂刑政固有先
後緩急之序要之亦不可以偏廢也使有禮樂
而無刑政則徒善不足以為治使有刑政而無
禮樂則徒法不能以自行故傳謂禮樂刑政四
===
達而不悖則王道備誠哉是言也稽之於古唐
虞之時以言其禮則五禮脩而三禮明以言其
樂則六律和而八音諧禮樂於是乎大備焉德
惟善政政在養民而六府三事之允治明于五
刑刑期無刑而五服三就之克允刑政於是乎
大彰焉是以當時萬邦協和而黎民有於變之
休庶績咸熙而四夷有來王之效豈非唐虞能
用禮樂刑政而致雍熙泰和之盛乎然推其所
由則又本於堯之允恭克讓舜之溫恭允塞之
所致也夏商之世司徒脩六禮以節民性樂正
punctuated:
莫善於樂。」是禮樂所以教民，而為出治之本，陛下所謂先與急者在是也。若夫政者，法制禁令也，所以一民之行，而率其倦怠焉；刑者，墨、劓、剕、宮、大辟也，所以防民之奸，而懲其恣肆焉。故曰：「道之以政，齊之以刑，民免而無耻。」是刑政所以弼教，而為輔治之具，陛下所謂後與緩者在是也。雖然，禮樂刑政固有先後緩急之序，要之亦不可以偏廢也。使有禮樂而無刑政，則徒善不足以為治；使有刑政而無禮樂，則徒法不能以自行。故傳謂：「禮樂刑政，四達而不悖，則王道備。」誠哉是言也！

稽之於古，唐、虞之時，以言其禮，則五禮備而三禮明；以言其樂，則六律和而八音諧，禮樂於是乎大備焉。「德惟善政，政在養民」，而六府三事之允治；「明于五刑」，「刑期無刑」，而五服三就之克允，刑政於是乎大彰焉。是以當時萬邦協和，而黎民有於變之休；庶績咸熈，而四夷有来王之效。豈非唐、虞能用禮樂刑政，而致雍熈泰和之盛乎？然推其所由，則又本於堯之「允恭克讓」、舜之「温恭允塞」之所致也。夏、商之世，司徒脩六禮以節民性，樂正
translation_en:
…none is better than music.” Thus rites and music are the means by which the people are instructed and serve as the foundation from which governance proceeds; what Your Majesty refers to as that which comes first and is urgent lies herein. As for administration, it consists of legal institutions, prohibitions, and ordinances, which are the means to unify the conduct of the people and rouse them from their indolence and negligence; as for punishments, they consist of tattooing, amputation of the nose, amputation of the feet, castration, and death, which are the means to guard against the wickedness of the people and chastise their unbridled license. Hence it is said: “Lead them by means of administration, keep them in line by means of punishments, and the people will evade them without having any sense of shame.” Thus punishments and administration are the means to assist instruction and serve as instruments to aid governance; what Your Majesty refers to as that which comes later and is less urgent lies herein. Even so, while rites, music, punishments, and administration certainly have an order of priority and urgency, in the final analysis none of them can be neglected in favor of the others. If there were rites and music without punishments and administration, then goodness alone would not suffice to effect governance; if there were punishments and administration without rites and music, then laws alone could not put themselves into practice. Therefore the commentary says: “When rites, music, punishments, and administration reach everywhere in all four directions without contradiction, then the Kingly Way is complete.” True indeed are these words!

Examining the matter in antiquity, in the time of Tang and Yu [Yao and Shun], if we speak of their rites, the Five Rites were complete and the Three Rites were made clear; if we speak of their music, the six pitch-standards were in harmony and the eight timbres were in accord—rites and music were thus grandly complete. “Virtue is seen in good administration, and administration lies in nourishing the people,” so that the Six Treasuries and Three Businesses were truly well-governed; “being clear about the Five Punishments” and “using punishments in the hope that there will be no punishments,” so that the five grades of punishments and their three places of execution were fittingly carried out—punishments and administration were thus grandly manifest. Therefore, at that time the myriad states were brought into harmony, and the black-haired people enjoyed the blessing of transformation; all achievements were resplendent, and the蠻 barbarians of the four quarters responded by coming to pay homage to the king. Was this not because Tang and Yu were able to employ rites, music, punishments, and administration, thereby bringing about the flourishing state of harmonious peace and great concord? Yet if we trace the source from which this arose, it was in turn rooted in Yao’s being “sincerely courteous and capable of yielding” and Shun’s being “gentle, respectful, and sincerely upright.” In the ages of Xia and Shang, the Minister of Education (situ) cultivated the Six Rites in order to regulate the nature of the people, and the Director of Music (yuezheng)…

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
崇四術以教士習立典則以貽子孫而有闗石
和鈞之設焉制官刑以儆有位而有三風十愆
之訓焉成周之世宗伯掌五禮以親萬民司樂
掌六樂以諧萬民司馬掌邦政以九法正邦國
司寇掌邦刑以三典詰四方情文備而制度詳
是以當時聲教四訖而兆民允殖丕冒海隅而
萬姓悅服豈非三代能用禮樂刑政而致雍熈
泰和之盛乎然原其所自則亦本於禹之允迪
厥德湯之咸有一德文武之純亦不已丕則敏
德之所致也夫唐虞三代以誠心行道而致治
===
效之盛如此後之有天下者莫如漢唐宋若高
祖之豁達大度文帝之恭儉玄默武帝之雄才
大略宣帝之綜核名實以至光武之沈幾先物
明帝之下身遵道章帝之左右藝文此漢之英
君誼辟也觀其用綿蕞所習之儀奏昭德五行
之舞制屯田而定租稅作九章而除肉刑其用
禮樂刑政也如此然或不事詩書或謙讓未遑
或內多寵慾或擇術不審又有吏事深刻察察
為明優柔不斷者求之當時雖有海內富庶幾
致刑措之風百姓寬息人賴其慶之美方之唐

punctuated:
崇四術以教士，習立典則以貽子孫，而有闗石和鈞之設焉；制官刑以儆有位，而有三風十愆之訓焉。成周之世，宗伯掌五禮以親萬民，司樂掌六樂以諧萬民，司馬掌邦政以九法正邦國，司寇掌邦刑以三典詰四方，情文備而制度詳。是以當時聲教四訖而兆民允殖，丕冒海隅而萬姓悅服，豈非三代能用禮樂刑政而致雍熈泰和之盛乎？然原其所自，則亦本於禹之允迪厥德、湯之咸有一德、文武之純亦不已、丕則敏德之所致也。夫唐虞、三代以誠心行道，而致治效之盛如此。
後之有天下者，莫如漢、唐、宋。若高祖之豁達大度，文帝之恭儉玄默，武帝之雄才大略，宣帝之綜核名實，以至光武之沈幾先物，明帝之下身遵道，章帝之左右藝文，此漢之英君誼辟也。觀其用綿蕞所習之儀，奏《昭德》、《五行》之舞，制屯田而定租稅，作《九章》而除肉刑，其用禮樂刑政也如此。然或不事《詩》《書》，或謙讓未遑，或內多寵慾，或擇術不審，又有吏事深刻、察察為明、優柔不斷者。求之當時，雖有海內富庶、幾致刑措之風，百姓寬息、人賴其慶之美，方之唐…
translation_en:
…exalted the Four Arts to instruct scholars; they established statutes and norms to bequeath to their descendants, wherein there was the institution of standard weights of the shi and jun; they formulated punishments for officials to warn those in office, wherein there were the admonitions against the Three Unwholesome Airs and Ten Faults. In the era of the flourishing Zhou, the Minister of Rites took charge of the Five Rites to bring the myriad people into亲密 harmony; the Director of Music took charge of the Six Musics to harmonize the myriad people; the Minister of War took charge of state administration, using the Nine Laws to rectify the states and domains; and the Minister of Justice took charge of state punishments, using the Three Penal Codes to scrutinize the four quarters. Sentiment and outward form were complete, and the institutional systems were detailed. Therefore, at that time their moral prestige and teachings reached in all four directions and the millions of people truly multiplied; their grand influence covered the corners of the seas and the myriad surnames gladly submitted. Was this not because the Three Dynasties were able to employ rites, music, punishments, and administration to bring about the flourishing of harmonious prosperity and supreme peace? Yet if we trace where this came from, it too was brought about by being rooted in Yu's sincerely walking in his virtue, Tang's possessing pure and constant virtue, and King Wen and King Wu's unceasing purity and grandly modeling themselves on diligent virtue. Now, Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties practiced the Way with a sincere mind, and thus brought about such flourishing governance and results.

Among those who possessed All-under-Heaven in later times, none equaled the Han, Tang, and Song. Such rulers as Gaozu with his broad-minded generosity, Emperor Wen with his reverent frugality and quiet non-action, Emperor Wu with his heroic talent and grand strategy, and Emperor Xuan with his comprehensive verification of name and reality, down to Guangwu with his deep foresight anticipating affairs, Emperor Ming with his humbling himself to follow the Way, and Emperor Zhang with his patronage of arts and letters—these were the heroic sovereigns and righteous rulers of the Han. Looking at how they employed the court ceremonial practiced with ropes and grass markers, performed the昭德 (Zhaode, Manifesting Virtue) and 五行 (Wuxing, Five Phases) dances, instituted state farms and fixed land taxes, and drew up the Nine Chapters of the legal code while abolishing corporal mutilation punishments—such was their use of rites, music, punishments, and administration! Yet some paid no heed to the Classic of Poetry and Classic of Documents, some modestly declined and found no leisure for礼樂, some harbored many favorites and desires within the palace, and some were uncritical in choosing their methods of rule; furthermore, there were those who were harsh and severe in administrative affairs, who mistook petty scrutiny for discernment, or who were overly gentle and indecisive. Looking at those times, although they had the customs of domestic enrichment and the near setting aside of punishments, and the admirable qualities of the common people enjoying relief and relying on their blessings, when compared with the [transformative influence] of Tang…

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
虞三代雍熈之化不啻碔砆之於美玉矣此無
他由其徒用禮樂刑政而行之不能本乎誠故
也若夫太宗之英邁絶倫玄宗之勵精圖治憲
宗之剛明果斷此唐之英君誼辟也觀其採古
制而定章服分二部以習音樂立府兵租庸調
之法除斷趾而增覆奏其用禮樂刑政也如此
然而一則假仁喜功一則惑於女色一則不終
其業考之當時雖有斗米三錢絶域来庭之盛
民皆樂業威令幾振之美揆之唐虞三代泰和
之治不啻魚目之厠美珠矣此無他由其徒尚
===
禮樂刑政而用之不能本乎誠故也迨夫有宋
之興太祖之仁義太宗之沈謀有以開創于前
真宗之英悟仁宗之仁恕有以守成於後真所
謂英君誼辟矣觀其定朝儀而詳服製正音律
而録名數嚴科禁以弭奢僭採勅條以為卷編
固皆用禮樂刑政以圖至治矣然或好微行或
傷恩義或假符瑞而封禪或以邪正而互用雖
曰治效有過於漢唐而亦不能比隆於唐虞三
代也詳其所以又豈非設誠於内者有或替歟
夫漢唐宋諸君不能誠心行道而治效不古若

translation_en:
… the harmonious and flourishing transformation of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties, it is no different from comparing a common agate-like stone (wufu) to fine jade. This is for no other reason than that they merely made use of rites, music, punishments, and governance, yet in practicing them could not root them in sincerity.

As for the unmatched heroic spirit of Taizong, the diligent dedication to governance of Xuanzong, and the firm, discerning decisiveness of Xianzong—these were the heroic lords and righteous rulers of the Tang. Looking at how they drew upon ancient institutions to fix official insignia and robes, divided musical performance into two sections to practice music, established the systems of garrison militia (fubing) and the threefold tax of grain, labor, and cloth (zuyongdiao), and abolished the amputation of feet while increasing the required reviews of capital sentences—such was their use of rites, music, punishments, and governance. Yet one of them feigned benevolence and delighted in martial exploits, one was deluded by female beauty, and one failed to carry his enterprise through to the end. Examining their eras, although there was the prosperity of a peck of rice costing only three cash and distant lands coming to pay court, and the excellence of the people all rejoicing in their livelihoods and imperial authority and ordinances being nearly revitalized, when measured against the supremely harmonious governance of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, it is no different from fish eyes mixed in among fine pearls. This is for no other reason than that they merely esteemed rites, music, punishments, and governance, yet in employing them could not root them in sincerity.

When we come to the rise of the Song dynasty, the benevolence and righteousness of Taizu and the deep counsel of Taizong enabled them to found the dynasty beforehand; the brilliant comprehension of Zhenzong and the benevolent forbearance of Renzong enabled them to preserve the achievements afterward—they were truly what are called heroic lords and righteous rulers. Looking at how they fixed court ceremonial and detailed the regulations for attire, rectified the musical pitches and recorded their categories and numbers, tightened statutory prohibitions to curb extravagance and usurpation, and gathered imperial edicts and articles to compile them into scrolls and volumes—all of these were indeed uses of rites, music, punishments, and governance to seek supreme order. Yet some were fond of traveling incognito, some harmed familial grace and duty, some made pretexts of auspicious omens to perform the feng and shan sacrifices, and some employed the crooked and the upright interchangeably. Although it may be said that the efficacy of their governance surpassed that of the Han and Tang, they still could not match the splendor of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Examining in detail why this was so, is it not again because the establishment of sincerity within had at times lapsed?

Now, how the various rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song were unable to practice the Way with a sincere heart, so that the efficacy of their governance did not equal that of antiquity…

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
者如此洪惟我
太祖高皇帝肇造區夏
太宗文皇帝肅清邦家而隆古之風以振
仁宗昭皇帝繼其統
宣宗章皇帝纂其功而隆古之治益彰所以然者固
不外乎禮樂刑政之用原其所以用禮樂刑政
又豈不本於
列聖至誠之心也哉
陛下應
天人之歸心嗣
===
祖宗之洪業復位以来孜孜圖治夙興夜寐不遑寧
處慮民性之未中也則用禮以節之慮民聲之
未和也則用樂以和之而禮也樂也固並舉而
無遺矣慮民行之不一也則脩政以一之慮民
姦之未息也則明刑以防之政也刑也亦並行
而不偏矣是以治效之盛曠古莫及而
聖心猶有治效未極于盛之慮臣有以知
陛下真大有為之君真不世出之主真可以四三王
六五帝而視漢唐宋諸君風斯下矣
陛下欲究禮樂之原臣則以為禮樂之原固不外乎

text:
一誠
陛下欲求刑政之本臣則以為刑政之本亦不外乎
一誠蓋真實無妄純粹不雜者誠也一有所雜
則偽而不誠矣悠久不息始終無間者誠也一
有所間則息而不誠矣
陛下運此心之誠以興禮樂則大禮與天地同節大
樂與天地同和而禮不失於慝樂不流於淫矣
陛下運此心之誠以用刑政則一政之出人皆信之
如蓍龜一刑之施人皆畏之如鈇鉞而政不失
於乖刑不流於慘矣禮樂刑政雖備舉而並行
===

必先禮而後樂先政而後刑此四者施行之次
序也行之既有其序則禮樂昭宣刑政脩舉極
天蟠地周流四達凡天下之民莫不是遵是守
而無違悖者矣然所以行而達之之要實本於

陛下能於禮樂刑政之用一本於誠則治化之盛又

之黎民與唐虞之黎民同一於變時雍矣今之
百姓與三代之百姓同一徧為爾德矣何則世

translation_en: …a single sincerity. Since Your Majesty wishes to seek the root of punishments and governance, your servant holds that the root of punishments and governance likewise lies in nothing other than a single sincerity. Now, that which is true and free from falsehood, pure and unadulterated, is sincerity; the moment there is any adulteration, it becomes false and is no longer sincere. That which is enduring and unceasing, without interruption from beginning to end, is sincerity; the moment there is any interruption, it ceases and is no longer sincere. If Your Majesty applies the sincerity of this mind to promote rites and music, then great rites will share the same measure as Heaven and Earth, great music will share the same harmony as Heaven and Earth, rites will not err toward evil, and music will not degenerate into licentiousness. If Your Majesty applies the sincerity of this mind to employ punishments and governance, then whenever a policy is issued, everyone will trust it like yarrow stalks and tortoise shells; whenever a punishment is applied, everyone will stand in awe of it like battle-axes and halberds, governance will not err toward perversity, and punishments will not degenerate into cruelty. Although rites, music, punishments, and governance are all fully instituted and practiced together, rites and music ought to come first, while punishments and governance ought to come after. Analyzed further, one must put rites first and music after, and put governance first and punishments after—this is the proper sequence for putting these four into practice. Once they are practiced according to their proper sequence, rites and music will be brightly manifested, punishments and governance will be well ordered and upheld, reaching to the highest heavens and spanning the earth, circulating everywhere and extending in all four directions, so that among all the people of the empire there will be none who do not follow and observe them, and none who disobey or rebel. Yet the essential key to practicing them and making them reach everywhere is truly rooted in the sincerity of a single thought of Your Majesty. 哉唐堯虞舜所以帝天下而致黎民於變者此
道也禹湯文武所以王天下而措斯世雍熙者
亦此道也後乎漢唐宋之治僅底於小康而不
能儗羨乎唐虞三代之盛者盧非此道之有未

李永通

臣對：臣聞為治必本於道，行道必本諸心。盖心者，一身之主宰、萬化之本原，而禮樂刑政之所由推也。推此心之和敬以制禮樂，則為治之大本以立；推此心之仁義以施刑政，則為治之大用以行。本立而用行，治天下之要道豈外乎此哉？唐堯、虞舜所以帝天下而致黎民於變者，此道也；禹、湯、文、武所以王天下而措斯世雍熈者，亦此道也。後乎漢、唐、宋之治，僅底於小康，而不能儷美乎唐、虞、三代之盛者，庸非此道之有未盡歟？

translation_en:
Li Yongtong 李永通

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that governance must be rooted in the Way, and practicing the Way must be rooted in the mind. For the mind is the master of the entire person, the fundamental source of the myriad transformations, and that from which rites, music, punishments, and administration are extended. When one extends the harmony and reverence of this mind to institute rites and music, the great foundation of governance is thereby established; when one extends the benevolence and righteousness of this mind to implement punishments and administration, the great function of governance is thereby carried out. When the foundation is established and the function is carried out, how could the essential Way of governing all under Heaven lie outside of this? That by which Yao of Tang and Shun of Yu ruled as emperors over all under Heaven and brought the black-haired people to transformation was this Way; that by which Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu ruled as kings over all under Heaven and placed the world in harmonious prosperity was also this Way. Why is it that in later times the governance of the Han, Tang, and Song merely attained lesser tranquility, and could not match the beauty of the flourishing ages of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—is it not because this Way was not yet fully exhausted?

Your servant reverently reflects that Your Majesty the Emperor is endowed with a disposition of keen intelligence and sagely wisdom, and is complete in the virtues of centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness, succeeding to the great line of succession and grandly unfolding vast plans. Previously, when You inherited the great succession and obligations, You did not approach sensual pleasures of music and beauty, and daily attended the Classics Colloquium to discourse upon and seek out ultimate principles; therefore, the imperial influence was pure and solemn, and governance and moral instruction were glorious and bright. Now that You have gloriously restored Yourself to the precious throne, the great Mandate is renewed; Your utmost filial piety reaches the spiritual and bright, and Your enriching favors abundantly fill the realm within the seas. The flourishing of Your transformative governance is truly sufficient to surpass Tang and Yu and excel the Three Dynasties. Yet You still embody the Way in humble modesty and do not presume to be self-satisfied; thus, in the leisure from Your myriad affairs of state, You have summoned Your servants to the court and graciously bestowed…

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
清問詢以禮樂刑政之實古今治效隆替之由而
求推行之序臣有以知
陛下之心即帝舜好問好察之心文王望道未見之
意也所以昭文明於萬世綿
國祚於無疆者端在是矣顧臣草茅賤質曷足以
上揆
淵衷然
聖謨洋洋臣敢不精白一心拜手稽首而對揚于萬
一乎臣伏讀
制策曰朕惟治天下亦多術矣舉而行之必有其
===
要傳謂禮樂刑政四達而不悖則王道備然則其
要固不出此四者而行之亦有先後緩急之序歟
臣聞為治有要莫先於禮樂輔治有法莫切於
刑政四者乃治天下之大經大法缺一不可也
是故辨貴賤而定民志莫大於禮聖人則法天
地自然之序而制為三千三百之禮焉然禮之
制雖多而其本則在於一心之敬而已格神人
而和上下莫先於樂聖人則法天地自然之和
而作為五音六律之樂焉然樂之文雖殊而其
本則在於一心之和而已禮以節

punctuated:
清問，詢以禮樂刑政之實、古今治效隆替之由，而求推行之序。臣有以知陛下之心，即帝舜好問好察之心、文王望道未見之意也。所以昭文明於萬世、綿國祚於無疆者，端在是矣。顧臣草茅賤質，曷足以上揆淵衷？然聖謨洋洋，臣敢不精白一心，拜手稽首而對揚于萬一乎？

臣伏讀制策曰：「朕惟治天下亦多術矣，舉而行之，必有其要。《傳》謂禮樂刑政四達而不悖，則王道備。然則其要固不出此四者，而行之亦有先後緩急之序歟？」臣聞為治有要，莫先於禮樂；輔治有法，莫切於刑政。四者乃治天下之大經大法，缺一不可也。是故辨貴賤而定民志，莫大於禮；聖人則法天地自然之序，而制為三千三百之禮焉。然禮之制雖多，而其本則在於一心之敬而已。格神人而和上下，莫先於樂；聖人則法天地自然之和，而作為五音六律之樂焉。然樂之文雖殊，而其本則在於一心之和而已。禮以節
translation_en:
… your pure inquiry, asking about the realities of rites, music, punishments, and administration, as well as the reasons for the flourishing and decline of effective governance from antiquity to the present, and seeking the proper sequence for putting them into practice. By this your servant knows that Your Majesty's heart is none other than the heart of Emperor Shun, who loved to ask and loved to examine, and the mind of King Wen, who looked toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it. That by which brilliant culture is made manifest for ten thousand generations and the dynasty's fortune is prolonged without bound truly lies right here. Yet considering that your servant is of humble, rustic substance, how could he be worthy of fathoming the depths of Your Majesty's mind above? Nevertheless, since the Sacred counsels are vast and grand, how could your servant dare not purify his heart with single-minded devotion, bow his head to his hands and to the ground, and set forth a reply in praise of even one part in ten thousand?

Your servant humbly reads the Imperial policy question, which says: "We reflect that there are indeed many methods for governing All under Heaven, yet in taking them up and putting them into practice, there must be essentials. The Commentary states that when rites, music, punishments, and administration reach everywhere without contradiction, then the Kingly Way is complete. If so, its essentials surely do not go beyond these four things, yet in practicing them is there also an order of priority and urgency?" Your servant has heard that in governing there are essentials, and none takes precedence over rites and music; in assisting governance there are laws, and none is more urgent than punishments and administration. These four are the great norms and grand laws for governing All under Heaven; not a single one can be lacking. Therefore, for distinguishing noble and base and settling the minds of the people, nothing is greater than rites. The sages modeled themselves on the natural order of Heaven and Earth and instituted the three thousand and three hundred rules of ritual. Yet although the institutions of ritual are numerous, their root lies simply in the reverence of a single heart. For reaching spirits and men and harmonizing superiors and inferiors, nothing takes precedence over music. The sages modeled themselves on the natural harmony of Heaven and Earth and created the music of the five tones and six pitch-pipes. Yet although the patterns of music are varied, their root lies simply in the harmony of a single heart. Rites serve to regulate…

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
聲二者乃為治之要在所當先而不可緩矣然
既以禮樂為教苟或有倦怠不率者又必輔之
以刑政政者正也所以正人之不正也聖人因
人之倦怠而政以正之使禮樂之教無不行所
謂紀綱法度之屬是已政不徒政必仁以出之
然後政得其宜焉刑者成也一成而不可變也
聖人因人之不率而刑以防之使禮樂之道無
或廢所謂墨劓剕宮大辟之類是已刑不徒刑
必義以制之然後刑得其當焉政以率其怠刑
以防其奸二者乃輔治之法在所當後而不可
===
急矣由是觀之則知禮樂刑政四者固治天下
之要道而其行之先後緩急又有叙而不可紊
者如此傳謂禮樂刑政四達而不悖則王道備
正此謂也臣伏讀
制策曰唐虞三代所以措天下於雍熈泰和之盛
者率用此道可歷指其實而詳言之歟後之有天
下者莫若漢唐宋其間英君誼辟亦有用此道者
其治效不足以比隆於唐虞三代者其故何歟臣
考諸唐虞之時禮有三禮五禮之異而節文以
辨樂有大章大韶之殊而神人以和政有養民

下者莫若漢唐宋其間英君誼辟亦有用此道者
其治效不足以比隆於唐虞三代者其故何歟臣
考諸唐虞之時禮有三禮五禮之異而節文以
辨樂有大韶之殊而神人以和政有養民
punctuated:
聲，二者乃為治之要，在所當先而不可緩矣。然既以禮樂為教，苟或有倦怠不率者，又必輔之以刑政。政者，正也，所以正人之不正也。聖人因人之倦怠而政以正之，使禮樂之教無不行，所謂紀綱、法度之屬是已。政不徒政，必仁以出之，然後政得其宜焉。刑者，成也，一成而不可變也。聖人因人之不率而刑以防之，使禮樂之道無或廢，所謂墨、劓、剕、宮、大辟之類是已。刑不徒刑，必義以制之，然後刑得其當焉。政以率其怠，刑以防其奸，二者乃輔治之法，在所當後而不可急矣。由是觀之，則知禮、樂、刑、政四者，固治天下之要道，而其行之先後緩急，又有叙而不可紊者如此。《傳》謂「禮樂刑政，四達而不悖，則王道備」，正此謂也。

臣伏讀制策曰：「唐、虞、三代所以措天下於雍熈泰和之盛者，率用此道，可歷指其實而詳言之歟？後之有天下者，莫若漢、唐、宋，其間英君誼辟，亦有用此道者，其治效不足以比隆於唐、虞、三代者，其故何歟？」臣考諸唐、虞之時，禮有三禮、五禮之異，而節文以辨；樂有《大章》、《大韶》之殊，而神人以和；政有養民
translation_en:
…sound [of music]. These two are the essentials of governance; they must be given priority and cannot be delayed. Yet once rites and music have been established as instruction, if there happen to be those who are negligent, indolent, or disobedient, one must also supplement them with punishments and administration. "Administration" (zheng) means "to rectify" (zheng)—that by which the unrectified in men is rectified. Because of men's negligence and indolence, the sages used administration to rectify them, ensuring that instruction in rites and music is carried out everywhere; what are called governing principles, laws, and regulations belong to this category. Administration is not merely administration; it must be issued forth with benevolence, and only then does administration attain its appropriateness. "Punishment" (xing) means "completion" (cheng)—once completed, it cannot be altered. Because of men's disobedience, the sages used punishments to guard against them, ensuring that the Way of rites and music is never abandoned; what are called tattooing, amputation of the nose, amputation of the feet, castration, and capital punishment belong to this category. Punishment is not merely punishment; it must be regulated with righteousness, and only then does punishment attain its proper measure. Administration is used to urge on the indolent, and punishment is used to guard against the wicked; these two are the methods that assist governance, which must come afterward and should not be rushed. Viewed from this perspective, we know that rites, music, punishments, and administration are indeed the essential Way for governing the world, and that the priority and urgency of their implementation have such an order that cannot be thrown into confusion. When the Commentary says, "When rites, music, punishments, and administration reach everywhere without contradiction, the Kingly Way is complete," this is precisely what it means.

Your servant humbly reads the Emperor's policy question, which says: "That whereby Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties placed the world into the flourishing state of harmonious and supreme peace was generally by employing this Way; can you point out the facts one by one and speak of them in detail? Among later rulers who possessed the world, none surpassed Han, Tang, and Song; among them were heroic sovereigns and righteous monarchs who also employed this Way, yet the efficacy of their governance was insufficient to rival the splendor of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—what is the reason for this?" Your servant has examined the times of Tang and Yu: in rites, there was the distinction between the Three Rites and the Five Rites, whereby ritual regulations and forms were differentiated; in music, there was the difference between the Dazhang and the Dashao, whereby spirits and men were brought into harmony; in administration, there was the nourishment of the people's…

之善而府事允治刑有弼教之美而就居克允
是以四方有風動之休萬國有咸寧之效而雍
熈泰和之治莫盛於此矣然唐虞以是道而致
治化之盛者無他焉以其有和敬仁義之心為
之本也三代之時質文異尚三綱五常禮之大
體商不能改乎夏周不能改乎商至於制度文
為隨時而損益故大而朝覲會同冠昏喪祭秩
秩乎其文小而禴祠烝嘗燕飲鄉射郁郁乎其
典禮之儀文備矣禹作大夏湯作大濩武王周
公亦作大武與勺焉語其器則鐘鼓管籥干戚
===
之有倫語其文則屈伸俯仰綴兆之有度樂之
聲容盛矣夏有典則之貽商有風愆之戒周以
六典治邦國以八法治官府以八柄馭羣臣以
八統馭萬民而政之施也益詳夏作禹刑商作
湯刑周以三典詰四方以五刑糾萬民以八辟

比屋有可封之俗人人有士君子之行而雍熈
泰和之治亦可謂盛矣然三代以是道而致治
化之盛者無他焉亦以其有和敬仁義之心為
之本也三代以下英君誼辟世未嘗無而禮樂

punctuated: 之善，而府事允治；刑有弼教之美，而就居克允。是以四方有風動之休，萬國有咸寧之效，而雍熈泰和之治，莫盛於此矣。然唐、虞以是道而致治化之盛者，無他焉，以其有和敬仁義之心為之本也。三代之時，質文異尚。三綱五常，禮之大體，商不能改乎夏，周不能改乎商；至於制度文為，隨時而損益。故大而朝覲、會同、冠、昏、喪、祭，秩秩乎其文；小而禴、祠、烝、嘗、燕飲、鄉射，郁郁乎其典，禮之儀文備矣。禹作《大夏》，湯作《大濩》，武王、周公亦作《大武》與《勺》焉。語其器則鐘、鼓、管、籥、干、戚之有倫，語其文則屈伸、俯仰、綴兆之有度，樂之聲容盛矣。夏有典則之貽，商有風愆之戒，周以六典治邦國，以八法治官府，以八柄馭羣臣，以八統馭萬民，而政之施也益詳。夏作《禹刑》，商作《湯刑》，周以三典詰四方，以五刑糾萬民，以八辟麗邦法，以九伐正邦國，而刑之制也益備。是以比屋有可封之俗，人人有士君子之行，而雍熈泰和之治，亦可謂盛矣。然三代以是道而致治化之盛者，無他焉，亦以其有和敬仁義之心為之本也。三代以下，英君誼辟，世未嘗無，而禮樂
translation_en:
… [administration had] the excellence of [nourishing the people], so the six treasuries and three affairs were truly well-governed; punishments had the beauty of assisting moral instruction, so the conviction and sentencing of criminals were met with sincere compliance [? 就居克允, for 五流有宅，五宅三居，惟明克允]. Therefore, the four quarters enjoyed the blessing of being moved as if by the wind, the myriad states experienced the effect of universal peace, and the governance of harmonious prosperity and supreme concord was never more flourishing than in this era. Yet the reason Tang and Yu achieved such flourishing governance and transformation through this Way was none other than that they took minds of harmony, reverence, benevolence, and righteousness as the foundation.

In the time of the Three Dynasties, simplicity and cultural refinement were variously esteemed. As for the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues—the great substance of ritual propriety—the Shang could not alter what came from the Xia, and the Zhou could not alter what came from the Shang; as for institutional regulations and cultural forms, they were abridged or augmented in accordance with the times. Thus, in great matters such as court audiences, general assemblies, capping, weddings, funerals, and sacrifices, how orderly was their cultural form! And in lesser matters such as the vernal, estival, hibernal, and autumnal ancestral sacrifices, banquets, and district archery rituals, how rich were their canons! The ceremonial forms of ritual propriety were complete indeed. Yu created the Great Xia (Daxia) music, Tang created the Great Hu (Dahu) music, and King Wu and the Duke of Zhou likewise created the Great Wu (Dawu) and the Shao music. Speaking of their instruments, the bells, drums, pipes, flutes, shields, and battle-axes had their proper order; speaking of their forms, the bending and stretching, bowing and looking up, and the positions and boundaries of the dancers had their proper measure: the sounds and appearances of music were flourishing indeed. The Xia bequeathed canons and models, the Shang had warnings against degenerate customs and faults, and the Zhou governed the states with the Six Canons, governed the official bureaus with the Eight Laws, controlled the multitude of officials with the Eight Prerogatives, and controlled the myriad people with the Eight Unifying Principles: thus the application of administration became ever more detailed. The Xia created the Punishments of Yu (Yu xing), the Shang created the Punishments of Tang (Tang xing), and the Zhou scrutinized the four quarters with the Three Penal Canons, corrected the myriad people with the Five Punishments, attached the Eight Deliberations to the laws of the state, and rectified the states with the Nine Punitive Expeditions: thus the system of punishments became ever more complete. Therefore, every household had customs worthy of enfeoffment, every person had the conduct of a scholar-gentleman, and the governance of harmonious prosperity and supreme concord could also be called flourishing indeed. Yet the reason the Three Dynasties achieved such flourishing governance and transformation through this Way was none other than that they too took minds of harmony, reverence, benevolence, and righteousness as the foundation.

為禮樂之原在乎和敬刑政之本在乎仁義而
仁義和敬實具乎一心心之所存久而不息治
未有不臻于盛者也臣不敢復有他說惟願
陛下推和敬之心以制禮樂則禮序樂和而為治之
本無不立推仁義之心以施刑政則政善刑中
而輔治之法無不備行之以序而積之以悠久
將見天下之人惟禮樂是遵是行而無一人之
或違惟政刑是式是懼而無一人之或悖群黎
百姓咸囿於甄陶之中四海八荒悉歸於防範
之內
===

之治效無異矣唐虞三代豈得專美於前哉此
其明效大驗所必至者臣是以惓惓於此不敢

translation_en:
…believe that the source of rites and music lies in harmony and reverence, and the root of punishments and governance lies in benevolence and righteousness; and benevolence, righteousness, harmony, and reverence are in fact all contained within the one mind. When what the mind preserves endures for a long time without ceasing, governance has never failed to reach the height of flourishing. Your servant dares not offer any other theories, wishing only that Your Majesty extend the mind of harmony and reverence to institute rites and music, so that the rites are orderly and music is harmonious, and the root of governance is in every way established; and extend the mind of benevolence and righteousness to administer punishments and governance, so that governance is good and punishments are just, and the laws that assist governance are in every way complete. If these are practiced in proper sequence and accumulated over a long duration, one will see the people of the world solely following and practicing rites and music, with not a single person transgressing them; and solely taking governance and punishments as their model and object of awe, with not a single person defying them. The multitude of common people will all be encompassed within your molding influence, and the four seas and eight wildernesses will all return within the bounds of your moral framework. Through this the August Ultimate will be established; through this kingly transformation will be made manifest; through this heaven, earth, and the myriad things will be given their proper place and nurtured; and through this auspicious omens and felicitous portents will gather side by side. The efficacy of governance today will be no different from the efficacy of governance in antiquity—how could Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties monopolize glory in the past? These are the clear results and grand proofs that must inevitably come to pass; therefore your servant is earnestly devoted to this and dares not broadly cite other theories to speak before Your Majesty.

As for the Way of rites, music, punishments, and governance, my investigation of it has not yet reached full detail, yet with my one humble insight, I venture to sully on high…

臣對臣聞帝王之治天下有其要而治天下之

而為禮樂刑政之本也漢唐宋之治所以不古
若者庸非禮樂刑政之施不能本於是心故歟
恭惟
===
皇帝陛下
稟聰明睿智之資
備聖神文武之德纘
列聖之洪圖紹帝王之道統道已至矣而不替謙沖
體道之誠治已隆矣而恒存勵精圖治之志乃
於
萬幾之暇特籲臣等旅進於
廷策以禮樂刑政首詢唐虞三代致治之實次及
漢唐宋治不逮古之由終則欲究禮樂刑政之
本臣有以知
punctuated:
臣鄭環。
臣對：臣聞帝王之治天下有其要，而治天下之要有其本。蓋禮、樂、刑、政四者，治天下之要道也；而行之必有其本焉。本者何？心是也。以是心而制禮，則禮無不備；以是心而作樂，則樂無不和；至於明刑、立政，亦必本於是心，然後刑清而政舉焉。唐、虞、三代之治所以極其盛者，能以是心而為禮、樂、刑、政之本也；漢、唐、宋之治所以不古若者，庸非禮、樂、刑、政之施，不能本於是心故歟？恭惟皇帝陛下，禀聰明睿智之資，備聖神文武之德，纘列聖之洪圖，紹帝王之道統。道已至矣，而不替謙冲體道之誠；治已隆矣，而恒存勵精圖治之志。乃於萬幾之暇，特籲臣等旅進於廷，策以禮、樂、刑、政，首詢唐、虞、三代致治之實，次及漢、唐、宋治不逮古之由，終則欲究禮、樂、刑、政之本。臣有以知

Your servant Zheng Huan 鄭環.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that the governance of all under Heaven by emperors and kings has its essentials, and the essentials of governing all under Heaven have their fundamental root. Now rites, music, punishments, and administration—these four are the essential ways of governing all under Heaven; yet in putting them into practice, there must be a fundamental root to them. What is this root? It is the mind-and-heart (xin). When one institutes rites with this mind, there is no rite that is not complete; when one creates music with this mind, there is no music that is not harmonious; and when it comes to clarifying punishments and establishing administration, they too must be rooted in this mind, and only then will punishments be pure and administration upheld. The reason the governance of Tang 唐 [Yao], Yu 虞 [Shun], and the Three Dynasties reached the utmost flourishing is that they were able to take this mind as the root of rites, music, punishments, and administration. And the reason the governance of Han 漢, Tang 唐, and Song 宋 did not match antiquity—was it not because their implementation of rites, music, punishments, and administration could not be rooted in this mind?

Reverently I reflect that Your Imperial Majesty is endowed with intelligent, perspicacious, and wise qualities, possesses sagely, spirit-like, civil, and martial virtue, continues the grand plan of the successive sagely ancestors, and inherits the transmission of the Way (daotong) of the emperors and kings. Your Way has already reached the utmost, yet You do not relax Your sincere humility in embodying the Way; Your governance is already flourishing, yet You constantly maintain the resolve to exert Yourself vigorously in seeking good rule. Thus, in the leisure from a myriad affairs of state, You have specially summoned Your servants to advance together in the court and posed a policy question on rites, music, punishments, and administration—first inquiring into the realities of how Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties achieved good governance, next touching upon the reasons why the governance of Han, Tang, and Song failed to reach antiquity, and finally wishing to investigate the fundamental root of rites, music, punishments, and administration. From this, Your servant knows that …

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
皇上之心即堯舜下詢芻蕘好問好察之心也臣雖
愚昧敢不精白一心以對揚
聖天子之休命乎臣伏讀
聖策有曰朕惟治天下亦多術矣舉而行之必有
其要傳謂禮樂刑政四達而不悖則王道備然則
其要固不出此四者而行之亦有先後緩急之序
歟臣惟帝王之治天下論其術固非一端舉其要
不過禮樂刑政四者而已聖人知安上治民莫
善於禮於是因天理之節文為人事之儀則而
有三千三百之條焉知移風易俗莫善於樂於
===
是因天地之和氣為聲音之節奏而有五聲六
律之目焉然禮以節民心樂以和民聲無非因
人之情而為之也豈非治天下之要道歟禮樂
作矣茍或倦怠而不行不可無政以率之聖人
於是立為法制禁令之政而有紀綱之布焉政
既舉矣茍或恣肆而不率不可無刑以防之聖
人於是定為墨劓剕宫大辟之刑而有三千之
属焉然政以行之刑以防之由是人皆禮樂是
遵而不敢廢也豈非治天下之要道歟傳曰禮
樂刑政四達而不悖則王道備信乎四者通行

皇上之心，即堯、舜下詢芻蕘、好問好察之心也。臣雖愚昧，敢不精白一心，以對揚聖天子之休命乎？

臣伏讀聖策有曰：「朕惟治天下亦多術矣，舉而行之，必有其要。《傳》謂：『禮、樂、刑、政，四達而不悖，則王道備。』然則其要固不出此四者，而行之亦有先後緩急之序歟？」臣惟帝王之治天下，論其術固非一端，舉其要不過禮、樂、刑、政四者而已。聖人知安上治民莫善於禮，於是因天理之節文，為人事之儀則，而有三千三百之條焉；知移風易俗莫善於樂，於是因天地之和氣，為聲音之節奏，而有五聲六律之目焉。然禮以節民心，樂以和民聲，無非因人之情而為之也，豈非治天下之要道歟？禮樂作矣，茍或倦怠而不行，不可無政以率之。聖人於是立為法制禁令之政，而有紀綱之布焉。政既舉矣，茍或恣肆而不率，不可無刑以防之。聖人於是定為墨、劓、剕、宫、大辟之刑，而有三千之属焉。然政以行之，刑以防之，由是人皆禮樂是遵而不敢廢也，豈非治天下之要道歟？《傳》曰：「禮、樂、刑、政，四達而不悖，則王道備。」信乎四者通行
translation_en:
… Your Majesty's mind is indeed the very mind of Yao and Shun, who inquired below even of grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers and delighted in questioning and examining. Though your servant is foolish and ignorant, how could he dare not purify and devote his whole heart to respond to and extol the illustrious mandate of the Sacred Son of Heaven?

Your servant humbly reads the Sacred Policy Question, which states: "We reflect that there are indeed many methods for governing All under Heaven, yet in taking them up and putting them into practice, there must be what is essential. The commentary states: 'When rites, music, punishments, and administration reach everywhere without contradiction, the Kingly Way is complete.' If this is so, then what is essential surely does not go beyond these four; yet in putting them into practice, is there also an order of priority and urgency?" Your servant reflects that when emperors and kings govern All under Heaven, if one discusses their methods there is surely more than a single way, yet if one sums up what is essential, it goes no further than the four matters of rites, music, punishments, and administration. The sages knew that for securing the position of superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than rites; thereupon, based on the gradations and refinements of heavenly principle, they established ceremonial rules for human affairs, and thus there were the three thousand major and three thousand minor articles. They knew that for shifting customs and changing habits, nothing is better than music; thereupon, based on the harmonious vital energy of Heaven and Earth, they established the rhythms and cadences of sound and tone, and thus there were the categories of the five notes and the six pitch-pipes. Yet rites serve to regulate the minds of the people, and music serves to harmonize the voices of the people; all of this is done in accordance with human feelings—is it not the essential way of governing All under Heaven? Once rites and music have been created, if people should become weary and lax and fail to practice them, one cannot do without administration to lead them. Thereupon the sages established administration consisting of laws, regulations, prohibitions, and ordinances, and thus there was the promulgation of guiding principles and institutional frameworks. Once administration has been instituted, if people should become willful and unrestrained and fail to follow it, one cannot do without punishments to guard against them. Thereupon the sages fixed the punishments of tattooing, nose-cutting, foot-cutting, castration, and death, and thus there were the three thousand offenses. Yet with administration to put them into practice and punishments to guard against violations, everyone thereby abides by rites and music and dares not abandon them—is this not the essential way of governing All under Heaven? title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
於天下而民無違悖之者治道之備可知矣夫
禮樂乃出治之本在所當先而為當務之急者
刑政乃輔治之具在所當後而為當務之緩者
其先後緩急如此又豈可紊其序哉臣又伏讀
聖策有曰唐虞三代所以措天下於雍熈泰和之
盛者率用此道可歷指其實而詳言之歟後之有
天下者莫若漢唐宋其間英君誼辟亦有用此道
者然而治效不能比隆於唐虞三代其故何歟臣
惟唐虞之世黎民於變而萬國咸寧三代之時
九圍是式而四海永清治效之盛曠古而無以
===
加矣所以然者亦惟用夫禮樂刑政以治之耳
觀其命伯夷典禮而上下以辨命后夔典樂而
神人以和大禹宅百揆而九功惟叙臯陶明五
刑而四方風動此唐虞禮樂刑政之實也夏有
夏禮殷有殷禮周則宗伯掌邦禮以五禮而安
邦國夏作大夏殷作大濩周則司樂掌邦樂以
六樂而諧萬民若夫夏商之政有典則之貽有
八政之齊而周則司馬掌邦政以詔王之法夏
商之刑有獄成之告有官刑之儆周則司寇掌
邦刑以佐王之典此三代禮樂刑政之實也究

punctuated:
於天下，而民無違悖之者，治道之備可知矣。夫禮樂乃出治之本，在所當先，而為當務之急者；刑政乃輔治之具，在所當後，而為當務之緩者。其先後緩急如此，又豈可紊其序哉？
臣又伏讀聖策有曰：「唐、虞、三代所以措天下於雍熈泰和之盛者，率用此道，可歷指其實而詳言之歟？後之有天下者，莫若漢、唐、宋，其間英君誼辟亦有用此道者，然而治效不能比隆於唐、虞、三代，其故何歟？」臣惟唐、虞之世，黎民於變而萬國咸寧；三代之時，九圍是式而四海永清，治效之盛，曠古而無以加矣。所以然者，亦惟用夫禮、樂、刑、政以治之耳。觀其命伯夷典禮，而上下以辨；命后夔典樂，而神人以和；大禹宅百揆，而九功惟叙；臯陶明五刑，而四方風動：此唐、虞禮、樂、刑、政之實也。夏有夏禮，殷有殷禮，周則宗伯掌邦禮，以五禮而安邦國；夏作《大夏》，殷作《大濩》，周則司樂掌邦樂，以六樂而諧萬民。若夫夏、商之政，有典則之貽，有八政之齊；而周則司馬掌邦政，以詔王之法。夏、商之刑，有獄成之告，有《官刑》之儆；周則司寇掌邦刑，以佐王之典：此三代禮、樂、刑、政之實也。究
translation_en:
…throughout All-under-Heaven, without the people defying or opposing them, one can see that the Way of governance is complete. Now, rites and music are the foundation from which governance issues; they belong to what must come first and are the urgent priorities of the task at hand. Punishments and administrative measures are the instruments that assist governance; they belong to what must come later and are the less urgent priorities of the task at hand. Since their sequence and relative urgency are such as this, how could one possibly disrupt their order?

Your servant again humbly reads Your Majesty's policy question, which says: "That whereby Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties placed All-under-Heaven into a flourishing state of harmonious peace and grand concord was invariably by employing this Way; can you point out the concrete realities one by one and speak of them in detail? Among those who possessed All-under-Heaven in later times, none surpassed Han, Tang, and Song; among them, illustrious rulers and righteous sovereigns also employed this Way, yet the efficacy of their governance could not compare in grandeur to that of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—what is the reason for this?" Your servant reflects that in the ages of Tang and Yu, the black-haired people were transformed and the myriad states were all at peace; in the time of the Three Dynasties, the nine divisions took them as their model and the four seas were forever clear. The flourishing efficacy of their governance was unprecedented since antiquity and could not be surpassed. The reason it was so is simply that they employed rites, music, punishments, and administrative measures to govern. Observe how Boyi 伯夷 was commanded to take charge of the rites, whereby superiors and inferiors were distinguished; Sovereign Kui 后夔 was commanded to take charge of music, whereby spirits and men were brought into harmony; the Great Yu 大禹 occupied the post of General Regulator (baikui), whereby the nine achievements were kept in order; and Gao Yao 臯陶 clarified the five punishments, whereby the four quarters were moved as by the wind: these are the concrete realities of the rites, music, punishments, and administrative measures of Tang and Yu. The Xia had the rites of Xia, the Yin had the rites of Yin, and in the Zhou, the Minister of Rites (zongbo) managed the rites of the state, using the five rites to bring peace to the states and realms. The Xia composed the Daxia (Great Xia) music, the Yin composed the Dahuo (Great Protection) music, and in the Zhou, the Director of Music (siyue) managed the music of the state, using the six musical performances to harmonize the myriad people. As for the administrative measures of Xia and Shang, there was the bequeathing of canons and standards, and the ordering of the eight objects of government; while in the Zhou, the Minister of War (sima) managed the administrative measures of the state in order to proclaim the laws of the king. As for the punishments of Xia and Shang, there was the reporting of completed judicial cases, and the warnings of the Offenses of Officials (Guanxing); while in the Zhou, the Minister of Justice (sikou) managed the punishments of the state in order to assist the statutes of the king: these are the concrete realities of the rites, music, punishments, and administrative measures of the Three Dynasties. translation_en: …Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao [the Hongwu Emperor] and Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen [the Yongle Emperor] founded the enterprise and handed down the tradition, achieving governance through rites, music, punishments, and administration in earlier times; Benevolent Ancestor Emperor Zhao [the Hongxi Emperor] and Proclaiming Ancestor Emperor Zhang [the Xuande Emperor] succeeded to the heritage and maintained the civil order, manifesting the efficacy of rites, music, punishments, and administration in later times. Sage has succeeded sage for nearly a hundred years now; governance and moral instruction are auspicious and bright, and the people and all things are prosperous and contented, no different indeed from the flourishing ages of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties. The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "The sage perseveres long in his Way, and all under Heaven is transformed and perfected." This is what is meant. Now Your Majesty has resumed the great enterprise and reascended the precious throne, preserving the mind of the ancestral line of sage emperors and seeking the governance of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, wielding heavenly vigor in sole decision-making and shining bright illumination upon the myriad affairs of state, dressing before dawn and eating late at night in order to plan for well-ordered rule. Knowing that the minds of the people cannot go unregulated, You use rites to regulate them; knowing that the voices of the people cannot go unharmonized, You use music to harmonize them. Administration is used to unify the conduct of the people, thereby rousing them from their indolence; punishments are used to guard against the wickedness of the people, thereby chastising their unruliness. Therefore, rites and music are brilliantly and fully instituted, while punishments and administration are clearly and simultaneously carried out. Among the people of the realm, there are none who do not turn in allegiance to rites and music, thereby following the pattern of the Sovereign, and none who do not stand in awe of punishments and administration, thereby walking the road of the King. In the flourishing efficacy of Your governance, You can match the distant ages of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—how could Han, Tang, [and Song]…

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
宋之足較哉然
皇上猶以為未極其盛者其不自滿假之心歟所謂
禮樂之原刑政之本不必他求惟在
皇上之一心耳盖禮樂者是心之中和也推是心之
中和而為禮樂則禮樂之原得矣刑政者是心
之制度也推是心之制度而為刑政則刑政之
本得矣雖然本原既得而行之又不可無其序
也盖禮樂所以出治而化民者刑政所以輔治
而禁民者必先節之以禮和之以樂而後正之
以政律之以刑如四時之運五行之布宣於四
===
方流於遠迩将見下民無一人之或梗無一動
之敢違信乎四達而不悖矣是以聲名洋溢乎
中國和氣充盈於宇宙天地位而萬物育夷狄
賓而四靈至百姓於是乎昭明黎民於是乎於
變則雍熈泰和之盛尚何異於唐虞三代也哉
聖策之終又曰子大夫潜心經史有年矣其詳著
于篇朕將採而用焉臣愚學術空疎識見寡陋已
摭所聞略陳於前矣敢於終篇復有獻焉盖禮
樂刑政之施雖本於心而心之所以能為禮樂
刑政之本者以其明德之不昧耳惟此心之德

punctuated:
宋之足較哉？然皇上猶以為未極其盛者，其不自滿假之心歟？所謂禮樂之原、刑政之本，不必他求，惟在皇上之一心耳。盖禮樂者，是心之中和也，推是心之中和而為禮樂，則禮樂之原得矣；刑政者，是心之制度也，推是心之制度而為刑政，則刑政之本得矣。雖然，本原既得，而行之又不可無其序也。盖禮樂所以出治而化民者，刑政所以輔治而禁民者。必先節之以禮、和之以樂，而後正之以政、律之以刑，如四時之運、五行之布，宣於四方，流於遠迩，将見下民無一人之或梗、無一動之敢違，信乎四達而不悖矣。是以聲名洋溢乎中國，和氣充盈於宇宙，天地位而萬物育，夷狄賓而四靈至，百姓於是乎昭明，黎民於是乎於變，則雍熈泰和之盛，尚何異於唐、虞、三代也哉！
聖策之終又曰：「子大夫潜心經史有年矣，其詳著于篇，朕將採而用焉。」臣愚學術空疎，識見寡陋，已摭所聞，略陳於前矣，敢於終篇復有獻焉。盖禮樂刑政之施雖本於心，而心之所以能為禮樂刑政之本者，以其明德之不昧耳。惟此心之德
translation_en:
… and Song dynasties be worth comparing with it? Yet Your Majesty still considers that it has not reached its utmost flourishing—is this not out of a mind that refuses to be self-satisfied? What are called the source of rites and music and the root of punishments and governance need not be sought elsewhere; they lie solely within Your Majesty's single mind. For rites and music are the equilibrium and harmony of this mind; if one extends the equilibrium and harmony of this mind to create rites and music, then the source of rites and music is attained. Punishments and governance are the institutional measures of this mind; if one extends the institutional measures of this mind to create punishments and governance, then the root of punishments and governance is attained. Even so, once the root and source are attained, in putting them into practice one cannot be without proper sequence. For rites and music are the means by which governance is brought forth and the people are transformed, whereas punishments and governance are the means by which rule is assisted and the people are restrained. One must first regulate them with rites and harmonize them with music, and only afterward rectify them with governance and discipline them with punishments. Like the revolution of the four seasons and the distribution of the Five Phases, when these are proclaimed throughout the four quarters and flow near and far, one shall see that among the common people below there is not a single person who is obstinate, nor a single action that dares to transgress—truly reaching in all four directions without contradiction! Therefore, renown overflows throughout the Central Kingdom, harmonious ether fills the universe, heaven and earth take their proper places and the myriad things are nurtured, the peripheral tribes submit as guests and the four numinous creatures arrive, the hundred surnames are thereby made bright and clear, and the black-haired people are thereby transformed in concord. How then would the flourishing of such concordant splendor and supreme harmony differ in any way from that of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties?
At the conclusion of Your Sacred Policy Question, You further state: "You gentlemen have immersed your minds in the Classics and Histories for years now; set forth your views in detail in your essays, and We shall select from and employ them." Your foolish servant, whose learning is empty and sparse and whose insight is meager and shallow, has already gathered what he has heard and briefly set it forth above, yet dares at the conclusion of this essay to offer one further word. Although the application of rites, music, punishments, and governance is rooted in the mind, the reason the mind is able to serve as the root of rites, music, punishments, and governance is simply that its luminous virtue is not obscured. Only when the virtue of this mind…

title: 天順四年進士登科錄
text:
既明然後用禮樂刑政以為治則新民之功著
矣論至於是有以知禮樂刑政固本於心而又
不可無其德也故曰雖有其位苟無其德不敢
作禮樂焉又曰德惟善政曰有德惟刑由是觀
之必德具於心則禮樂可興刑政可舉帝王之
治可並
祖宗之業可宏可以開太平於悠久可以緜
宗社於無疆天下萬世斯民之大幸也顧臣之愚
不足以與天下計謹以一得之見上塵
聖覽干冒
===
天威不勝竦息之至臣謹對

治可並

聖覽干冒
天威不勝竦息之至臣謹對
punctuated: 既明，然後用禮樂刑政以為治，則新民之功著矣。論至於是，有以知禮樂刑政固本於心，而又不可無其德也。故曰：「雖有其位，苟無其德，不敢作禮樂焉。」又曰：「德惟善政。」曰：「有德惟刑。」由是觀之，必德具於心，則禮樂可興，刑政可舉，帝王之治可並，祖宗之業可宏，可以開太平於悠久，可以緜宗社於無疆，天下萬世斯民之大幸也。顧臣之愚，不足以與天下計，謹以一得之見，上塵聖覽。干冒天威，不勝竦息之至。臣謹對。
translation_en: … is first made luminous, and only then does one employ rites, music, punishments, and government to achieve order, then the achievement of renewing the people becomes manifest. Reasoning to this point, one knows that while rites, music, punishments, and government are indeed rooted in the mind, one also cannot be without its virtue. Therefore it is said: "Even though one holds the position, if one lacks the virtue, one dares not institute rites and music." And it is also said: "Virtue alone is good government." And it is said: "Only the virtuous should administer punishments." Viewed from this perspective, virtue must be complete within the mind; then rites and music can be made to flourish, punishments and government can be instituted, the governance of the ancient emperors and kings can be rivaled, and the enterprise of the Imperial Ancestors can be enlarged. Thus one can inaugurate Great Peace for ages to come and perpetuate the Dynastic Altars without end—this would be the great fortune of the people of the world for ten thousand generations! Yet in my foolishness, I am unworthy to participate in the counsels of the realm; I respectfully offer up this single humble insight to sully Your Sacred Gaze. For offending the Heavenly Majesty, I am overcome with trembling and awe. Your servant respectfully replies.
